sources.label: ChromeStatus feature 5484282563919872 — Android IME media insertion
Clipboard API Living Standard §5.2.4 — the paste event

inventory.name: IME media insertion delivered through the existing paste event (ClipboardEvent.clipboardData image items)

syntax.rationale: This change adds no new API ('No new Web API is needed', #why), so the page's declaration surface is the existing call form in the #example block: document.addEventListener('paste', handler), then event.clipboardData?.items, item.type and item.getAsFile() — the event the Clipboard API Living Standard §5.2.4 defines as the one the user agent fires 'When a user initiates a paste action'. The fragment contains the semantic <pre><code> block; there is no grammar, flag, or option bag to document.

inputs.rationale: #what-this-means-for-developers documents the input the site receives: the same paste-event DataTransfer that carries clipboard pastes ('Site listening for paste + reading DataTransfer' → 'Clipboard pastes + IME media insertions'). Nothing is passed by the developer and no new argument, dictionary, or permission is introduced — the page's own wording is that media 'arrives via existing clipboard/paste event pipeline' — so the input contract is the unchanged ClipboardEvent the site already reads.

outputs.rationale: The page's output-side surface is in the #example block: each image item yields a File/Blob through item.getAsFile() (null-checked with `if (!blob) continue`), which becomes a blob: URL and is appended as an to #editor. That the media arrives in the site's own paste handler is the observable result the page documents; the feature itself returns nothing to script.

errors.rationale: The page documents no error or exception path: delivery reuses the existing paste event, whose failure handling is the site's own handler code, and the ChromeStatus record lists no error surface. The nearest failure-shaped text in this fragment is the no-op row ('Sites not listening for paste' → 'No change'), which is a non-delivery case rather than a documented error contract — flagged in notes instead of claimed as documented.

context.rationale: #at-a-glance fixes the exposure context: Chrome 149 (stepped rollout), Android only, behavioural (no API change), with Firefox and Safari recorded as 'No signal' — matching the record's ff and safari views of 'No signal' (fetched 2026-10-07).

lifecycle.rationale: #why documents the delivery transition the feature adds: 'When an IME commits media content, Chrome converts it and delivers it to the page using the existing paste event / InputEvent path', so the sequence is IME commit on Android (commitContent) → Chromium conversion → paste event dispatched to the focused editable element → the site's handler. The same fragment states no object is constructed, registered, or torn down by the page, so no teardown lifecycle exists — the delivery rides an event the page never creates.

examples.rationale: #example is the page's only runnable example: a paste listener that filters image/* items, calls getAsFile(), and appends the result to #editor, shipped as a semantic <pre><code> block whose closing comment ties the handler to the Android keyboard's GIF/sticker key.

compatibility.rationale: #browser-support carries the page's third table: Chrome 149+ (Android) 'Stepped rollout' against 'No signal' for Firefox (Android) and Safari (iOS), with the note that the path is Android only and uses the existing clipboard event path — the record's ff/safari views are both 'No signal' (fetched 2026-10-07). The 149 side of the table is the case recorded as a divergence in notes.

securityPrivacy.rationale: Not documented by this page rather than absent in principle: the page carries no security or privacy statement — no permission, consent, origin, or sanitisation boundary — so nothing here establishes a sourced security/privacy contract, while the record it cites reports security_review_status and privacy_review_status both 'Pending' (fetched 2026-10-07). The nearest boundary text, that only pages listening for paste receive the media, is a delivery fact. Flagged in notes.

notes: B3 unit under gendn-g8o (2026-10-07). WHAT WAS ADDED: the page carried zero id attributes, so no selector could resolve; five ids were added to the EXISTING <h2> headings — at-a-glance (context), why (lifecycle), what-this-means-for-developers (inputs, and the two flagged-dimension anchors), example (syntax, outputs, examples), browser-support (compatibility) — and nothing else changed: git diff is five attribute additions, no rewording, no restructuring, no new prose, no styling. The ids sit on the heading elements because fragmentAfterId() slices to the next h1-h3 and this page has no h3. SURFACE: a behavioural platform change with no new web-facing API (the page states 'No new Web API is needed'), so the inventory is one item — the existing paste-event delivery of IME media — and no second surface is invented. SOURCES RE-FETCHED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-10-07): (1) https://chromestatus.com/feature/5484282563919872 → HTTP 200, but that URL serves a 3710-byte client-rendered app shell, so every record value quoted here was read from the machine-readable endpoint https://chromestatus.com/api/v0/features/5484282563919872 (HTTP 200; the body carries the XSSI prefix )]}' before the JSON). Its name is 'Android IME media insertion' and its summary is 'This feature allows IMEs to insert media content such as images, gifs and stickers into the Chrome Browser in Android.', so the record is this feature. (2) https://w3c.github.io/clipboard-apis/#clipboard-event-paste → HTTP 200; §5.2.4 reads 'When a user initiates a paste action, the user agent fires a clipboard event named paste. The event fires before any clipboard data is inserted into the document. If the cursor is in an editable context, the paste action will insert clipboard data in the most suitable format (if any) supported for the given context. The paste action has no effect in a non-editable context, but the paste event fires regardless.' DIVERGENCE FOUND, BOTH SIDES, NOT ADJUDICATED: the page's #at-a-glance reads 'Shipped in: Chrome 149 (Stepped rollout)' and 'Status: Stepped rollout (gradually enabled)', and #browser-support reads 'Chrome 149+ (Android): Stepped rollout'; the record's own status field reads 'Proposed' (browsers.chrome.status.text 'Proposed', milestone_str 'Proposed') with flag false, origintrial false, and desktop/android/webview/ios ALL null — no per-platform milestone is set on the record. The record's only 149 datum is a stage of stage_type 1061 (created 2026-04-16) with rollout_milestone 149, rollout_platforms ['1'], desktop_first 149, android_first null. Evidence on the page's side: the milestone listing https://chromestatus.com/api/v0/features?milestone=149 (fetched 2026-10-07) files this feature under the heading 'Stepped rollout' (that bucket holds exactly one feature — this one — alongside 13 'Enabled by default', 4 'Origin trial', 7 'In developer trial'), so 'Stepped rollout' is corroborated by a second endpoint even though the record's status enum still says 'Proposed'. The page carries no disclosure sentence; reported to the implementer rather than resolved here, since the disclosure sentence and its pin in scripts/source-disagreement.test.mjs are the implementer's call. UNRESOLVED OBSERVATION, NOT TREATED AS A CONTRADICTION: the page reads 'Platform: Android only' while that 149 stage carries rollout_platforms ['1'] with desktop_first 149 and android_first null. I could not resolve the rollout_platforms value set from any public artifact reachable here — other features carry ['3'] (5551475195904000 'Unframed display mode for IWAs', 5075144470036480 'Window Shape API'), ['7'] and ['6'] on successive milestones (5140168270413824 'Device Bound Session Credentials'), and ['1','3','5','6','7','8'] (5152728072060928 'Local network access restrictions'), while both GoogleChrome/chromestatus and GoogleChromeLabs/chromestatus are HTTP 404 and the record's rollout_plan_displayname is the generic 'Will ship enabled for all users' — so ['1'] cannot be read as 'desktop' or as 'Android' and I did not record this as a contradiction. Flagged for the implementer. DIMENSIONS THAT COULD NOT BE DOCUMENTED FROM THIS PAGE (flagged, not smoothed over): errors — marked not-applicable with the gap stated in its rationale (no error/exception path is documented; the only failure-shaped text is the no-op row for sites without a paste listener); securityPrivacy — marked not-applicable with the gap stated in its rationale (the page carries no security/privacy statement at all, and the record reports security_review_status and privacy_review_status both 'Pending'), a disclosure-level gap the implementer may want to close rather than a truthful 'documented'. CITATION COVERAGE (ratchet): scripts/check-citation-links.mjs's detector reports zero unlinked labels on this page (5 citation spans, each carrying an <a>; the prose pass strips <pre>/<code>), so this unit ADDED NO hrefs — the only hrefs it relies on are the two source links above, both verified HTTP 200 with curl -sL -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'. Two labels the ratchet does not flag are left for the implementer (out of this unit's scope): #why names the Android API `InputConnection.commitContent()` in <code> without a link (https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/inputmethod/InputConnection#commitContent(android.view.inputmethod.InputContentInfo,%20int,%20android.os.Bundle) → HTTP 200), and #example reads DataTransferItem.type / getAsFile(), which the cited Clipboard API §5.2.4 does not define (they live in the HTML Standard: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dnd.html#dom-datatransferitem-getasfile → HTTP 200).
